transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-09-03
Start: 14:30 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom (recording)
Notes: initial discovery for isolated-network / no internet private deployment; attendees from Redwood and Horizon Biotech

Summary (auto-generated, may be terse):
Horizon Biotech evaluating a fully isolated private deployment for regulated genomics workload. Key concerns: offline update process, hardware sizing (GPUs and NVMe), KMS/HSM integration for sealed media, SOC/ISO evidence, telemetry (minimal/air-gapped), and support model for on-site emergencies. Red flags: strict maintenance windows, long procurement lead times, and requirement for zero outbound connections from inference nodes.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Ava Kim: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Ava from Redwood Inference. Diego my solutions engineer is here, and lena may pop in for CSM context. How's everyone doing?
[00:07] Dr. Priya Nair: Good, thanks. I think we've got about an hour, we've blocked the time for a deep scoping.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Yeah, appreciate you making time. We're trying to nail down whether we can run Redwood in our isolated lab clusters — zero outbound network, monthly offline patches, that sort of thing.
[00:22] Diego Martinez: Great, thanks Marcus. We'll run fast — scope first, then security, then ops. Can you give a quick description of the target workload and latency expectations?
[00:31] Ethan Park: Sure — inference for variant calling pipelines. Peak QPS is low ~20 qps but bursts up to 80 for batch ingest windows. Latency requirement for interactive tools is sub-500ms 95th for short prompts, but many runs are long sequences (6k tokens) for batch analysis.
[00:48] Imran Qureshi: We also have strict data residency — none of the model or inference logs can leave the cluster. We have to keep everything on-prem for audit.
[00:56] Ava Kim: Okay, that helps. A few quick clarifying questions: do you need model training on prem or just serving? Also, do you expect offline updates to the model artifacts or periodic software updates?
[01:08] Dr. Priya Nair: Serving only. Models will be shipped as vetted artifacts from our research team. Updates will be monthly but sometimes ad-hoc for security patches.
[01:16] Sofia Alvarez: And compliance note — we require audit logs, immutable storage for certain logs, and we want to see evidence of SOC 2 or ISO attestation.
[01:25] Diego Martinez: Understood. Redwood's Private deployment supports customer-controlled control plane with options for air-gapped installs. We support sealed media updates and KMS/HSM integration for key wrapping. Quick caveat that some telemetry features are disabled in fully isolated mode.
[01:41] Marcus Lee: That lines up. A few practical constraints — our racks are limited to 10U for inference nodes, we prefer 4x A100 style nodes or equivalent; we want NVMe-backed cache for KV store and ability to tolerate a drive failure (RAID or replication).
[01:55] Diego Martinez: Cool. For long sequences, KV cache fits on NVMe; our sizing spreadsheet will recommend capacity based on token window and concurrent users. We'll share that.
[02:05] [00:02:05] (ambient noise)
[02:10] Imran Qureshi: On update process, explain how Redwood handles a monthly security patch when there is no internet. Do you provide signed images on removable media?
[02:18] Lena Vo: I can take that, we've done this with two other regulated customers. The standard is: Redwood packages a signed, encrypted bundle (tar+signature) that you import via removable encrypted disk. We support offline signing with customer KMS/HSM or our signing plus customer verification — depends on your compliance stance.
[02:33] Dr. Priya Nair: We would need customer-side signing via our HSM. External signing is a no-go.
[02:38] Diego Martinez: That's fine — we can work with your HSM workflow. We also support a deterministic verification step that runs locally and validates signatures before installation.
[02:48] [00:02:48] Speaker 5: (inaudible)
[02:51] Ava Kim: On support — two models: we can provide an on-site playbook and remote 'air-gap-safe' SSH agent you run locally, or we can provide an optional advisory on-call engineer who ships with physical tokens for emergency releases. Both are contractual.
[03:07] Marcus Lee: The remote agent is interesting but we cannot allow outbound SSH from the cluster. The SSH agent would need to be brokered through a jump appliance in our DMZ that you don't manage.
[03:19] Diego Martinez: Absolutely — we've done jump-bastion patterns. We also have a 'push-install' that you run from a controlled workstation in the DMZ that pulls the signed artifact from an internal file share then injects into the isolated network via an approved media pipeline.
[03:34] Ethan Park: Can Redwood's runtime run without any external model registry calls?
[03:37] Diego Martinez: Yes, the private package contains everything — model weights, tokenizer, config, and runtime. The runtime can be configured to never attempt outbound calls.
[03:45] Dr. Priya Nair: About telemetry: we need a way to collect operational metrics for capacity planning but we cannot allow logs to leave the cluster. Can you do aggregated, scrubbed reports we can export manually?
[03:57] Lena Vo: We provide an export tool that produces an encrypted metrics bundle you can transfer out via physical media. We also have a toggle to remove PII and to limit metric granularity. In fully air-gapped mode, no auto telemetry is sent by default.
[04:11] [00:04:11] (keyboard clack)
[04:14] Imran Qureshi: Hardware procurement — our purchasing takes months. Do you publish a support matrix for GPU types and recommended firmware?
[04:22] Diego Martinez: Yes, we'll share a hardware compatibility and tested-firmware matrix. For long sequences and KV hits, we recommend size for NVMe and a GPU with at least 80GB HBM for large models, or MxM2 quantized variants if you're constrained.
[04:36] Marcus Lee: Clarify the quantization question: if we choose int8/4-bit variants for cost, are there any differences in the offline update path?
[04:45] Diego Martinez: No difference operationally. The model artifact just contains quantized weights. The key complexity is validating quality — we recommend a canary stage on a small internal benchmark before wide rollout.
[04:55] Dr. Priya Nair: Canary on an isolated cluster — we can dedicate a small node pool for that.
[04:59] Ava Kim: Sounds good. Let's go into security and compliance specific asks — Sofia, want to pull up your list?
[05:05] Sofia Alvarez: Yes, quick bullets: SOC 2 type II report, ISO 27001 certificate if available, data retention and deletion proofs, evidence of KMS/HSM compatibility, audit log immutability, least privilege RBAC, and ability to support third-party pen tests.
[05:20] Diego Martinez: We can provide SOC 2 type II and our security whitepaper. ISO 27001 is in progress — we can provide interim artifacts. Regarding HSM, we support both PKCS#11-compatible HSMs and customer-managed cloud KMS if you allow a hybrid onboarding step. For immutable logs we recommend append-only object store mounts or WORM configurations on your storage.
[05:40] Imran Qureshi: We will not permit a hybrid step that calls out to the cloud. Everything must be local.
[05:44] Diego Martinez: Understood. In that case we recommend on-prem HSM that supports offline key wrapping and a local verification service.
[05:52] [00:05:52] (crosstalk)
[05:55] Ava Kim: A couple of operational questions: patch cadence — you said monthly, and ad-hoc for critical patches. Do you have blackout windows?
[06:03] Marcus Lee: Yes — for core production we have a maintenance window Saturday 02:00-06:00 local. For the research lab we can be more flexible but changes to production must be tested.
[06:12] Ava Kim: Perfect, we'll note that. For rollback, Redwood supports instant rollback to previous runtime and model artifacts if the update is applied via our installer. But you should plan for a tested rollback path at least once pre-prod before prod rollout.
[06:26] Ethan Park: What's the size of the runtime install? We have limited root disk on some nodes.
[06:31] Diego Martinez: The runtime plus one model can vary — for large models it can be 200-600GB depending on quantization and cache. NVMe cache is recommended to avoid writing to root.
[06:40] Imran Qureshi: About support SLAs: in a zero outbound cluster we need guaranteed on-site response time for P1s within 24-48 hours. Can Redwood commit?
[06:49] Ava Kim: We offer an enterprise plan with on-site support add-on; timelines depend on contract and geography — we can propose 24/48-hour windows for your site in the contract. We'll include that in the proposal.
[06:58] [00:06:58] (brief pause)
[07:02] Marcus Lee: One more thing: we need to understand the license and telemetry footprint — does the runtime phone home for licensing?
[07:10] Diego Martinez: No phone-home by default in private air-gapped mode. Licensing is handled via signed entitlement files that you host locally. We can do time-limited entitlements with offline renewal via new signed tokens.
[07:21] Dr. Priya Nair: Excellent. On the model side: we have internal IP in models and tokenizer vocab; we want assurance that no model artifacts are exfiltrated.
[07:31] Ava Kim: Our private deployment design keeps model artifacts local; we can add environment-level guards and strict file ACLs. We also do local checksum verification during install.
[07:40] [00:07:40] Speaker (unknown): (laughs) Okay good
[07:43] Sofia Alvarez: For audits we'll need a runbook showing update steps, who approves, and checklist for signature verification.
[07:50] Diego Martinez: We have runbook templates. We'll send a sanitized version you can adapt.
[07:55] Ava Kim: Let's discuss an example offline update flow and I'll document it in the follow-up: 1) Redwood builds signed artifact -> 2) artifact delivered to Horizon via SFTP to approved staging -> 3) Horizon signs with HSM (or verifies) -> 4) artifact loaded into isolated network via removable media and installed -> 5) local verification and health checks -> 6) optional metrics export. Any missing steps?
[08:20] Imran Qureshi: Need to include chain-of-custody for media and a checksum reconciliation step post-transfer.
[08:27] Diego Martinez: Good call — we'll include chain-of-custody and tamper-evident packaging in the playbook.
[08:33] [00:08:33] (phone ping)
[08:36] Marcus Lee: On resource constraints — if we can't fit a single 80GB HBM GPU, can we run a sharded approach across multiple smaller GPUs?
[08:45] Diego Martinez: Yes — sharded model serving is supported but comes with some latency tradeoffs. For your interactive 500ms goal, sharded across multiple 40GB GPUs may be risky at high concurrency. We'll show expected latency curves in the sizing sheet.
[08:59] Dr. Priya Nair: Could you include a benchmark for both single node 80GB vs 2x40GB sharded?
[09:05] Diego Martinez: Yes, we'll include sample benchmarks and also previous customer numbers for similar workloads.
[09:10] Ava Kim: Quick question for procurement — Marcus, any constraints on vendor packaging? Do you require factory-sealed drives or can we accept encrypted USB modules?
[09:19] Marcus Lee: Factory-sealed preferred for production. For lab we can use encrypted USB labeled and chain-of-custody logged.
[09:26] [00:09:26] (typing)
[09:29] Ethan Park: About backups — do you recommend local snapshotting for models and config?
[09:33] Diego Martinez: Yes: immutable snapshots on a separate storage tier and offline replication to an air-gapped vault are recommended. We'll include recommended retention.
[09:41] Sofia Alvarez: Pen test: we will likely want to run a third-party pentest post-install. Do you support that?
[09:47] Diego Martinez: Yes, with a non-disclosure and coordination window. We'll provide a contact for scoping.
[09:52] [00:09:52] (faint echo)
[09:54] Ava Kim: We're approaching time. Let's surface risks: long procurement lead times, limited rack space, strict blackout windows, and HSM integration complexity. Any others?
[10:06] Imran Qureshi: Also dependency on NVMe supply — long lead times for enterprise NVMe at scale.
[10:11] Marcus Lee: Also our legal team will require indemnities for IP leakage — that's a negotiation point.
[10:18] Diego Martinez: Understood, we can work through legal. On the technical side, we'll prepare a mitigation plan for each risk.
[10:25] Ava Kim: Recap of next steps: we'll send the security checklist and SOC artifacts, Diego will send the hardware sizing and benchmark examples, and we'll schedule a 2-hour on-site readiness workshop week of Sep 15. Marcus and Sofia will share compliance matrix and vendor constraints.
[10:42] Dr. Priya Nair: Sounds good. One last thing — do you have references for other life-science customers who have done air-gapped installs?
[10:50] Ava Kim: Yes, we have two redacted case studies. We'll share contacts with NDA.
[10:55] [00:10:55] Marcus Lee: Great, thanks everyone.
[10:57] Ava Kim: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the checklist and the sheets.
[11:01] (meeting ends)

Artifacts referenced:
